notes: NHRA = nhra_cougar.json (rows under the COUGAR, XR-7, COUGAR XR-7 and ELIMINATOR headings, all Cougar trims); NHRA is never listed in "sources". All Mercury/Ford/Lincoln-Mercury material (brochures, dealer booklets, product-change notices, brochure text reproduced on CCA pages, the Ford Torino power-team page) counts as ONE manufacturer source. Wikipedia articles (Mercury Cougar, Ford FE/335/385/Windsor engine) count as ONE source. EPA (1984 on) supports displacement, cylinder count and induction only. Statuses: confirmed = NHRA + 2 or more independent non-NHRA sources for the engine that year (hp from a non-NHRA source where one exists, otherwise the note says "hp rests on NHRA"); three_sources_not_nhra = 3 independent non-NHRA sources; two_sources_not_nhra = only 2 found (1983); nhra_only = NHRA row not backed by others; disputed = engine confirmed but the rating splits with no factory tie-breaker (alternatives in hp_alternatives). HP is gross through 1971 and SAE net from 1972. RPO/VIN codes are given only where a source states them; otherwise blank. Not recorded as entries: the 271-hp 289 Hi-Po that Over-Drive lists for 1967 (not in the 1967 Mercury power-team table, Wikipedia or Hagerty; unverified), and the 1999-2000 Roush Cougar (a dealer appearance/suspension package). Unreachable: HowStuffWorks (empty 202 responses) and the Hagerty valuation tool (login). No Mercury engine data was found online for 1979, 1983 or 1986, and OCR failed on the 1984, 1988, 1991, 1994, 1996, 1997 and 1999 Cougar brochures, so those years rest on the club, KBB, Wikipedia and EPA sources.
